transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because people keep telling me I’m not listening. Like my supervisor or my wife will be talking right to me, and then a minute later I realize I only got maybe half of what they said. Then I’m asking them to repeat it, and it’s causing problems.
Have you had trouble focusing and staying on task like this since you were a kid, or is this something that started more recently?

No, it’s been like this since I was a kid. I remember teachers moving my seat around because I couldn’t stay in one place, and I’d call out answers without waiting. I’d get in trouble for butting into other kids’ work too, even before middle school.
These days, do you still notice things like feeling restless, having trouble sitting still, or blurting things out/interrupting people, or has that mostly gone away as you got older?

Yeah, it’s definitely still there. If I have to sit still, it feels like this pressure building up in my chest and my legs, like I need to move or do something right then. If I don’t, I feel like I’m going to crawl out of my skin.
Have you been feeling unusually anxious, worried, or down lately, or noticed any other big changes in your mood or energy?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get frustrated because of all this, but I haven’t noticed some big change in my mood or energy or anything like that.
Would you say these attention and restlessness issues are causing real problems in more than one area of your life—like both at work and at home—or is it mostly noticeable in just one setting?

It’s definitely more than one place. At work it’s gotten serious—I’ve had formal warnings, and I honestly worry I could lose my job or mess something up on the line and cause a safety problem.

And at home, it causes problems too. My wife and kids get frustrated because I end up disrupting routines instead of helping things go smoothly.
Do you currently use any caffeine, nicotine, alcohol, or other substances regularly, and have you ever used stimulant drugs?
I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I don’t really have anything specific to report off the top of my head. When you say stimulant drugs, do you mean prescribed stuff, or illegal drugs, or both?

To clarify, I mean any use at all—whether it's caffeine, nicotine, alcohol, recreational drugs, or any stimulant medication you might have taken with or without a prescription. Do you currently or have you ever used any of these regularly?
I’m not really sure. I don’t have anything specific I can think of that I use regularly or anything like that. I’d have to think about it more, but nothing is standing out to me right now.
How many hours of sleep do you typically get each night, and do you feel rested when you wake up?
I’m not really sure, honestly. I haven’t been tracking how many hours I sleep. Some mornings I feel okay, other mornings not so much, but I don’t have a clear pattern I can point to.
Do you often lose or misplace things you need, like keys, tools, or paperwork, or find yourself forgetting appointments and tasks you were supposed to do?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I probably misplace stuff sometimes like anyone does, but I don’t have a clear example or pattern in mind. Same with appointments or tasks—I can’t say for sure that it happens often.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or activities—like keeping projects in order, managing multiple steps, or finishing things you start—at work or at home?

I’m not sure. I don’t really have a clear example of that. At work I just do what’s in front of me, and at home… I guess some things don’t get finished right away, but I couldn’t say if it’s a big problem or more than normal.
Do you often make careless mistakes or find it hard to keep your focus on tasks or details, like when doing paperwork, following instructions, or working on a project?

Yeah… that happens at work. On the line, I’ll rush through the quality checks and miss small stuff, like a wrong label or a fitting that isn’t tightened right. Then my supervisor has to pull me aside about it, because it’s not just once—it keeps happening.

Thinking back to before you were about 12 years old, can you recall specific examples—like report cards, teacher comments, or incidents at home—that showed these attention or restlessness problems were already present at that age?

Yeah, I can remember that from when I was little. Before middle school, teachers were always moving my seat because I couldn’t sit still or I’d bother other kids. I’d call out answers without waiting, and I got in trouble for jumping into other kids’ work or butting in when I wasn’t supposed to. It was pretty much a regular thing.
